answer_from_documents.description: Answer a question using only the documents you give it, such as help-center articles or search results, with citations saying which document backs up each part of the answer.

mock_response.answer: Refunds are issued within 5 business days.

sources.document: Refunds are issued within 5 business days of approval.

answer_from_documents.name: answer_from_documents

parameters.description: What to answer, such as 'How long do refunds take?'
parameters.name: question

parameters.description: The texts to answer from, one per entry: articles, policy sections, search results, or rows from an earlier step. Citations name them by position, counting from 1.
parameters.name: documents

parameters.description: How to answer, such as 'Reply in two sentences' or 'Say you do not know when the documents do not cover it'.
parameters.name: instructions

parameters.description: Which Cohere model does the work. Command A+ suits most jobs.
parameters.name: model

options.label: Command A Reasoning (thinks before it answers)

parameters.description: The most tokens the response may use; a token is about three-quarters of a word. Leave blank to use the model's own maximum output length.
parameters.name: max_tokens

parameters.description: Whether a reasoning model (Command A+ or Command A Reasoning) thinks before it answers. Thinking is slower, and it counts against the maximum response length. Other models never think. Off works as expected on Command A Reasoning; Command A+ then reasons inside its answer instead.
parameters.name: thinking

citations.description: Each passage of the answer the documents back up.

document_positions.description: Which documents back them up, by position from 1.

end.description: Where those words end in the answer.

start.description: Where those words start in the answer, from 0.

text.description: The words in the answer that the documents back up.

cited_positions.description: The positions of the documents cited, from 1.

finish_reason.description: COMPLETE when it finished, MAX_TOKENS when it was cut off, STOP_SEQUENCE when it stopped at a stop word.

is_grounded.description: Whether any document backs up the answer.

sources.description: The documents cited, in the order given.

citation_count.description: How many passages of the answer cite it.

position.description: The document's position in the list given, from 1.

was_cut_off.description: Whether it hit the maximum response length.

ask_about_image.description: Ask a Cohere vision model a question about one or more pictures: describe a photo, read a chart or a table, or answer a question about a scanned document.

mock_response.answer: A monarch butterfly resting on a pink flower.

ask_about_image.name: ask_about_image

parameters.description: The pictures to look at: upload them, pick files from an earlier step, or paste public web addresses. PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF (other formats are converted), up to 20.
parameters.name: images

parameters.description: What to ask about the pictures. Leave blank for a detailed description.
parameters.name: question

parameters.description: Which Cohere model looks at the pictures. Command A Vision answers at once; Command A+ thinks first, which can take a while.
parameters.name: model

options.label: Command A Vision (answers at once, recommended)

parameters.description: How closely to look. High reads small print but uses more tokens; Low is faster and cheaper.
parameters.name: detail

parameters.description: The most tokens the response may use; a token is about three-quarters of a word. Leave blank to use the model's own maximum output length.
parameters.name: max_tokens

parameters.description: Whether a reasoning model (Command A+ or Command A Reasoning) thinks before it answers. Thinking is slower, and it counts against the maximum response length. Other models never think. Off works as expected on Command A Reasoning; Command A+ then reasons inside its answer instead.
parameters.name: thinking

finish_reason.description: COMPLETE when it finished, MAX_TOKENS when it was cut off, STOP_SEQUENCE when it stopped at a stop word.

image_count.description: How many pictures it looked at.

was_cut_off.description: Whether it hit the maximum response length.

classify_text.description: Have a Command model pick the one category that fits a piece of text, such as routing a support email, and say why. The answer is always exactly one of the categories you list.

mock_response.reason: The customer asks for their money back.

classify_text.name: classify_text

parameters.description: The text to classify, such as an email, a review or a support ticket.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: The categories to choose from, one per entry. The step always returns exactly one of them, spelled as you wrote it.
parameters.name: categories

parameters.description: Rules for borderline cases, such as 'Anything that mentions money back is a Refund request'.
parameters.name: instructions

parameters.description: Which Cohere model decides. Command A+ suits most jobs.
parameters.name: model

count_tokens.description: Count how many tokens a text is for a Cohere model, to check a prompt fits before sending it or to estimate what it will cost.
count_tokens.name: count_tokens

parameters.description: The text to count, up to 65,536 characters.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: The model whose tokens to count: each family splits text its own way. Defaults to command-a-plus-05-2026.
parameters.name: model

character_count.description: How many characters the text is.

model.description: The model whose tokens were counted.

token_count.description: How many tokens the text is.

tokens.description: The tokens, as the numbers the model reads.

create_embeddings.description: Turn texts into vectors with Cohere Embed for semantic search, deduplication, clustering or classification, ready to store in a vector database such as Pinecone or Qdrant.
create_embeddings.name: create_embeddings

parameters.description: The texts to turn into vectors, one per entry. Each gives one vector, in the same order; up to 1,000.
parameters.name: texts

parameters.description: Embed what you store as 'Documents to search' and what you look things up with as 'Search queries': Cohere makes the two kinds to match each other.
parameters.name: input_type

parameters.description: Which Embed model to use. Match the model already used for any vectors you will compare these with.
parameters.name: model

parameters.description: Shorter vectors take less storage. Embed 5 and Embed 4 can be shortened; the older models always give their own length.
parameters.name: dimensions

dimensions.description: How many numbers each vector has.

embeddings.description: One vector per text, in the same order.

input_type.description: What the texts were embedded as.

extract_data.description: Pull the fields you name out of text or pictures, such as the total on a photographed receipt or the sender's company in an email, ready for a spreadsheet row or a CRM record. A field the material does not mention comes back empty, never guessed.
extract_data.name: extract_data

parameters.description: The text to pull the fields out of, such as an email or an invoice. Leave blank when the images hold everything.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: Pictures to read: upload them, pick files from an earlier step, or paste public web addresses. PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF (other formats are converted), up to 20.
parameters.name: images

parameters.description: The pieces of information you want, one per entry. Add what each means after a colon to steer it: 'total: the amount due in dollars'.
parameters.name: fields

parameters.description: Extra rules, such as 'Write dates as YYYY-MM-DD'.
parameters.name: instructions

parameters.description: Which Cohere model reads the material. Pictures need Command A+ or Command A Vision.
parameters.name: model

parameters.description: Instead of 'Fields', paste a JSON Schema whose root is an object, for numbers, lists or nested fields. Every object in it must list its required fields. When set, 'Fields' is ignored.
parameters.name: json_schema

data.description: The fields, by the names asked for.

missing_fields.description: The fields the material did not mention.

generate_model_response.description: Send a prompt to a Cohere Command model and get back its written response, as text or as a JSON object a later step can read field by field.

mock_response.response_text: Here is a thoughtful response to your question about artificial intelligence and its applications in modern software development.

generate_model_response.name: generate_model_response

parameters.description: The message or question to send to Cohere.
parameters.name: prompt

parameters.description: Which Cohere model writes the response. Command A+ suits most jobs; Command A Reasoning thinks first, for harder problems; Command R7B is the fastest. Defaults to command-a-plus-05-2026.
parameters.name: model

options.label: Command A Reasoning (thinks before it answers)

parameters.description: The most tokens the response may use; a token is about three-quarters of a word. Leave blank to use the model's own maximum output length.
parameters.name: max_tokens

parameters.description: How the model should behave, such as 'Answer in one short paragraph' or 'You are a friendly support agent for Acme'.
parameters.name: instructions

parameters.description: From 0 (focused and repeatable) to 1 (most varied). Leave blank for Cohere's default of 0.3.
parameters.name: temperature

parameters.description: Whether a reasoning model (Command A+ or Command A Reasoning) thinks before it answers. Thinking is slower and uses more tokens, and comes back separately from the response. Other models never think. Off works as expected on Command A Reasoning; Command A+ then reasons inside its answer instead.
parameters.name: thinking

parameters.description: Choose 'A JSON object' to get the response as data, in 'data'. Say in the prompt which fields the object should have.
parameters.name: reply_format

data.description: The response as a JSON object, when the response format is A JSON object.

finish_reason.description: COMPLETE when it finished, MAX_TOKENS when it was cut off, STOP_SEQUENCE when it stopped at a stop word.

response_text.description: The text that Cohere generated for your prompt.

thinking.description: The model's reasoning, when it thought first.

was_cut_off.description: Whether it hit the maximum response length.

get_model.description: Look up one Cohere model: what it is for, how much text it takes in, the abilities it has and whether it is deprecated.
get_model.name: get_model

parameters.description: The model to look up. Pick one, or type its name, such as command-a-plus-05-2026.
parameters.name: model

context_length.description: The most tokens it can take in at once.

default_for.description: The endpoints it is Cohere's default model for.

endpoints.description: What it can be used for: chat, embed, rerank and so on.

features.description: Extra abilities, such as tool use, vision or JSON output.

is_fine_tuned.description: Whether it is a fine-tuned model.

name.description: The model's name, to use in any Cohere step.

sampling_defaults.description: The settings it uses when a request leaves them out, such as temperature.

list_models.description: List the Cohere models this API key can use, with what each is for, how much text it takes in and the abilities it has.
list_models.name: list_models

parameters.description: Only models that do this.
parameters.name: endpoint

model_names.description: Every model's name, in the same order.

context_length.description: The most tokens it can take in at once.

default_for.description: The endpoints it is Cohere's default model for.

endpoints.description: What it can be used for: chat, embed, rerank and so on.

features.description: Extra abilities, such as tool use, vision or JSON output.

is_fine_tuned.description: Whether it is a fine-tuned model.

name.description: The model's name, to use in any Cohere step.

parse_document.description: Turn a PDF, a scan or a photo of a document into Markdown with Cohere Parse, keeping its reading order, lists and tables, and describing its pictures. Reads up to 20 pages a step.
parse_document.name: parse_document

parameters.description: The PDF or page image to parse: upload a file, pick one an earlier step produced, or paste a link to one.
parameters.name: document

parameters.description: For a PDF, the first page to parse. Leave blank to start at page 1.
parameters.name: first_page

parameters.description: For a PDF, the last page to parse. Leave blank to go to the end; a step parses up to 20 pages.
parameters.name: last_page

markdown.description: Every page parsed, as one Markdown text.

description.description: What the picture shows, in Cohere's words.

id.description: How the page's Markdown refers to the picture, such as img-0.

markdown.description: The page as Markdown, with tables as HTML.

rerank_documents.description: Order a list of texts or records by how well each answers a question, best first, with a score from 0 to 1. Useful for picking the passages or rows to hand an AI step.

mock_response.query: What is the capital of France?

results.document: Paris is the capital of France.
The Loire is France's longest river.

mock_response.top_document: Paris is the capital of France.

rerank_documents.name: rerank_documents

parameters.description: What you are looking for, written as a question or a search.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: The texts or records to rank, one per entry; up to 1,000. Records are ranked on all of their fields.
parameters.name: documents

parameters.description: Keep only the best matches. Leave blank to rank them all.
parameters.name: top_n

parameters.description: Which Rerank model to use.
parameters.name: model

document.description: The document's text, as Cohere ranked it.

position.description: Where it was in the list given, starting at 1.

top_position.description: Where the best match was in the list, from 1.

top_score.description: The best match's score, from 0 to 1.

transcribe_audio.description: Write down what is said in a recording with Cohere Transcribe, in any of 14 languages. Takes MP3, WAV, FLAC or OGG recordings of up to 25 MB.

mock_response.text: Thanks for calling Acme support, how can I help you today?

transcribe_audio.name: transcribe_audio

parameters.description: The recording to transcribe: upload a file, pick one an earlier step produced, or paste a link to one.
parameters.name: recording

parameters.description: The language being spoken. Cohere Transcribe does not detect it, so pick the one the recording is in.
parameters.name: language

parameters.description: Which Cohere Transcribe model listens.
parameters.name: model

language.description: The language listened for, as a code.

translate_text.description: Translate text into another language with Command A Translate, Cohere's model built for translation in 23 languages, or North Small Translate for more than 50.

mock_response.translation: Los reembolsos se emiten en un plazo de 5 días hábiles.

translate_text.name: translate_text

parameters.description: The text to translate.
parameters.name: text

parameters.description: The language to translate into, such as Spanish, Japanese or Brazilian Portuguese.
parameters.name: target_language

parameters.description: The language the text is in. Leave blank to let the model tell.
parameters.name: source_language

parameters.description: How to translate, such as 'Keep a formal tone' or 'Leave product names in English'.
parameters.name: instructions

parameters.description: Which Cohere model translates.
parameters.name: model

finish_reason.description: COMPLETE when it finished, MAX_TOKENS when it was cut off, STOP_SEQUENCE when it stopped at a stop word.

source_language.description: The language it was translated from, if given.

target_language.description: The language it was translated into.

was_cut_off.description: Whether it hit the maximum response length.

description: Use Cohere's Command, Embed, Rerank, Parse and Transcribe models in your workflows. Generate text, answer questions from your documents with citations, extract data, classify and translate text, and read images; create embeddings and rank documents for semantic search; and turn recordings and PDFs into text.
